FAQ.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.q1: What is the AWS Student Community Day?
FAQ.a1: It's a free one-day event organized by students and backed by AWS. It includes technical talks, hands-on workshops, networking sessions, and professional development opportunities in cloud technologies.
FAQ.a2: Everyone! The event is open to students, professionals, tech enthusiasts, and anyone interested in cloud computing. No prior experience required.
FAQ.a3: Yes, the event is completely free. You just need to register to reserve your spot as seating is limited.
FAQ.a4: Your laptop (if you want to participate in hands-on labs), charger, and a great attitude to learn. We recommend creating an AWS Free Tier account before the event.
FAQ.a5: Snacks and beverages will be provided during breaks. Catering details will be confirmed later.
FAQ.q6: How do I get to the venue?
FAQ.a6: The event will take place at Centro Histórico y Cultural "Juan de Dios Bátiz" (Manuel Carpio, Agricultura, Miguel Hidalgo, 11360 Mexico City, CDMX, At IPN). You can check out the exact location on the map.
FAQ.q7: Will talks be in Spanish or English?
FAQ.a7: Most talks will be in Spanish, but some may be in English. Site content is available in both languages.
FAQ.q8: Will there be a live stream or virtual track?
FAQ.a8: No, all talks and workshops at AWS Student Community Day Mexico-CDMX 2026 will be held 100% in person at Centro Histórico y Cultural "Juan de Dios Bátiz" at IPN.
FAQ.q9: How can I become a speaker?
FAQ.a9: You can submit your talk or workshop proposal through our official Call for Speakers at [Apply as Speaker](/en/speakers/postular). We welcome technical sessions, AWS architectures, and hands-on workshops.
FAQ.a10: Absolutely! The student volunteer call is open. You can join our team to support logistics, registration, and event operations by completing the [Volunteer Application Form](/en/voluntarios).
FAQ.q11: How can my tech or student community participate?
FAQ.a11: We are looking for tech communities and student groups to join as official partner allies to share the event, host collaborative activities, or provide mentors. Submit your proposal using our [Community Application Form](/en/comunidades).
FAQ.q12: How can my company or institution sponsor the event?
FAQ.a12: We offer various tiers and booth spaces for companies looking to connect with top university cloud talent. Check out the sponsorship deck and get in touch at our [Sponsorship Section](/en/sponsors).
FAQ.lead: What people ask us most before the event. If something is missing, write to us.

CodeOfConduct.title: Code of Conduct
CodeOfConduct.intro: The AWS Student Community Day Mexico-CDMX is governed by the AWS Community Code of Conduct. This event is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment for all participants, regardless of gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, age, religion, nationality, or experience level.
CodeOfConduct.purpose: This code of conduct outlines our expectations for all those who participate in our community, as well as the consequences of unacceptable behavior. We invite all those who participate in the AWS Student Community Day to help us create safe and positive experiences for everyone.
CodeOfConduct.expected_1: Participate in an authentic and active way, contributing to the health and longevity of the community.
CodeOfConduct.expected_2: Exercise consideration and respect in your words and actions.
CodeOfConduct.expected_4: Refrain from demeaning, discriminatory, or harassing behavior and speech.
CodeOfConduct.expected_5: Be mindful of your surroundings and of your fellow participants. Alert the organizers if you notice a dangerous situation, someone in distress, or violations of this code of conduct.
CodeOfConduct.expected_6: Respect the event spaces and equipment provided.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_1: Violence, threats of violence, or violent language directed against another person.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_2: Sexist, racist, homophobic, transphobic, ableist, or otherwise discriminatory jokes and language.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_3: Posting or displaying sexually explicit or violent material.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_4: Posting or threatening to post other people's personally identifying information ("doxing").
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_5: Personal insults, particularly those related to gender, sexual orientation, race, religion, or disability.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_6: Inappropriate photography or recording without consent.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_7: Inappropriate physical contact. You should have someone's consent before touching them.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_8: Unwelcome sexual attention, including sexualized comments or jokes, inappropriate physical contact, and unwelcome sexual advances.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_9: Deliberate intimidation, stalking, or following (online or in person).
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_10: Advocating for or encouraging any of the above behavior.
CodeOfConduct.unacceptable_11: Sustained disruption of community events, including talks and presentations.
CodeOfConduct.reporting: If you are subject to or witness unacceptable behavior, or have any other concerns, please notify an event organizer as soon as possible. Organizers are identified with visible badges during the event. You can also send a report to:
CodeOfConduct.consequences: Anyone asked to stop unacceptable behavior is expected to comply immediately. If a participant engages in unacceptable behavior, event organizers may take any action they deem appropriate, including temporary or permanent expulsion from the event without warning or refund.
CodeOfConduct.scope: This code of conduct applies to all AWS Student Community Day Mexico-CDMX spaces, both digital and in-person at IPN, as well as in one-on-one communications related to the event.
CodeOfConduct.aws_reference: This code of conduct is based on the AWS Community Code of Conduct.
CodeOfConduct.aws_reference_link: View the AWS Code of Conduct

PrivacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPolicy.intro: This Privacy Policy describes how AWS Student Builder Groups Mexico-CDMX (hereinafter, "we" or "the Organizer"), responsible for organizing the AWS Student Community Day Mexico-CDMX, collects, uses, stores, and protects the personal data of participants, speakers, volunteers, and website visitors.
PrivacyPolicy.controller: AWS Student Builder Groups of Mexico-CDMX, organizers of the AWS Student Community Day Mexico-CDMX 2026.
PrivacyPolicy.data_collected_intro: We collect the following personal data through our registration forms, speaker applications, and volunteer applications:
PrivacyPolicy.data_collected_4: AWS Student Builder Group membership (if applicable)
PrivacyPolicy.data_collected_5: Relevant professional information (LinkedIn profile, technical experience)
PrivacyPolicy.purpose_intro: The personal data collected will be used for the following purposes:
PrivacyPolicy.purpose_2: Sending relevant event information (confirmations, reminders, updates).
PrivacyPolicy.purpose_4: Generating participation certificates and QR access codes.
PrivacyPolicy.purpose_5: Producing anonymous statistics about attendance and participation.
PrivacyPolicy.purpose_7: Sharing your data with event sponsoring companies, exclusively with your express consent and for cloud technology marketing purposes.
PrivacyPolicy.sponsors:
With your prior, express and informed consent — given at registration — the personal data indicated (full name, email address and educational institution) may be shared with the sponsoring companies of AWS Student Community Day Mexico-CDMX 2026, solely for marketing communications about cloud technology products, services and opportunities.

This transfer requires your consent under the Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties, and the data may only be used for the stated purpose. The companies receiving it take on the same obligations as the Organizer regarding its processing.

This consent is optional — you can register without giving it. You may revoke it at any time, without retroactive effect, by writing to the address in the Contact section.
PrivacyPolicy.legal_basis: Personal data processing is governed by the Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (published 20 March 2025), its Regulations, and article 16 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States, which recognises the protection of personal data as a fundamental right. The basis for processing is the free, specific and informed consent you give when completing the forms. This document is the event's comprehensive privacy notice.
PrivacyPolicy.transfer: Your data is stored and processed on servers outside Mexico-CDMX, mainly on Amazon Web Services infrastructure in the United States, and with the providers we use to send email and host the site. These providers act as processors on behalf of the Organizer, so these transfers do not require additional consent.
PrivacyPolicy.retention: We keep your data for as long as it is needed for the purposes described, and at most two (2) years from the date of the event. After that it is deleted, unless a legal obligation requires keeping it longer. You can ask us to delete it sooner.
PrivacyPolicy.rights_intro: Under the Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties, you have the right to (ARCO rights):
PrivacyPolicy.rights_1: Access your personal data and the details of how it is processed.
PrivacyPolicy.rights_2: Rectify data that is inaccurate, incomplete or out of date.
PrivacyPolicy.rights_3: Cancel your data when you consider it is no longer needed for the stated purposes.
PrivacyPolicy.rights_4: Object to the processing of your data for specific purposes. If you believe your request was not handled, you may turn to the competent data protection authority.
PrivacyPolicy.rights_5: Withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out beforehand.
PrivacyPolicy.rights_6: Access your personal data that has been processed, free of charge.
PrivacyPolicy.contact: To exercise your rights or make any inquiry related to the processing of your personal data, you may contact us at the following email address:
PrivacyPolicy.changes: We reserve the right to modify this Privacy Policy at any time. Changes will be posted on this page with the date of the last update. We recommend that you periodically review this policy to stay informed about how we protect your personal data.
